name: Undersea cables & GPS
value: No new cable cut found to 19 Nov
summary: No new undersea cable cut or major GNSS jamming escalation found to 19 Nov; Baltic cable cases still in the courts
state: Searches on 19 Nov found no new undersea cable cut and no major new GNSS jamming escalation. Baltic cable cases from 2023–2025 are still before courts, including the Eagle S case returned for trial by the Helsinki Court of Appeal on 27 Aug (Daily Signal, 16 Nov), and Finland's court jailed the Fitburg's captain on 5 Nov over the 31 Dec 2025 damage. With recent incidents and legal follow-up but no fresh cut, Watch is kept rather than lowered.
for_you: Internet and power links around the Baltic remain under heightened watch. Disruption to consumers from a single cable fault is usually limited because traffic reroutes; pilots and mariners should follow official navigation notices on GNSS interference.
rubric_hit: Watch: recent cable damage incidents still being prosecuted; no new cut or confirmed sabotage found to 19 Nov

sources.title: Daily Signal — The Baltic's security battle is moving underwater

why: Subsea cables carry ~99% of intercontinental data; GPS jamming affects aviation and shipping.
drivers: Anchor drags, sabotage, conflict-zone jamming and spoofing.

rubric.alert: Multiple cable cuts isolating a region, or confirmed sabotage.
rubric.watch: Cable damage incident, or widespread GNSS interference affecting aviation.
rubric.normal: No new cable cuts or major jamming escalations.
